newsitem.title: UK: British economist overjoyed at Nobel Prize.
newsitem.headline: British economist overjoyed at Nobel Prize.

text.p: British professor James Mirrlees said on Tuesday he was overjoyed and "full of glee" at winning the Nobel Prize for Economics.

Mirrlees, who won the award jointly with Canadian William Vickrey, said he was shocked to receive the call telling of the prize. "It was extraordinary. My second thought was to check that the call was genuine," he told Reuters in an interview.
Mirrlees, speaking by phone from Cambridge University as colleagues came in to congratulate him, said he planned to celebrate this evening with a dinner of college friends.
Mirrlees, building on the work of Vickrey whom he has never met, has spent his life theorising on what is the optimum tax level that maintains a person's incentive to work.
He said the most exciting moment of his life came "when I finally cracked the optimal tax problem. It was really exciting to solve a problem, a bit embarrassing to get a prize".
"It came in a flash and it was very satisfactory. That was in 1968," he said.
